source.title: OthelloGPT learned a bag of heuristics

page_placements.theme: Rule-like neurons in small game- or task-trained models (OthelloGPT, Sudoku, DRL agents, numeric succession)

record.tranche_reason: The study reports neuron-level findings in a toy Othello network, but does not test any of the specified claim versions about Qwen3, other language models, InceptionV1, attribution graphs, or explanation scoring.
record.gate_note: The study reports mechanistic and causal findings about OthelloGPT neurons. These do not test the claim versions as defined; the toy-network findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study reverse-engineers OthelloGPT, a 25M-parameter transformer trained on Othello move sequences. It finds rule neurons, board-pattern neurons and clock neurons. It runs no audit of the share of neurons with one main job in any language model, and no vision-model study, attribution-graph comparison or explanation-scoring test. Its neuron findings concern a toy board-game model and fit no version as written.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors' best guess is that OthelloGPT computes board state and legal moves through a bag of independent, localized heuristics. They cannot rule out a succinct algorithm running alongside these rules.
record.recipe_differences: This is a mechanistic study of an Othello-playing toy transformer, using neuron classifiers, circuit analysis, and ablations; it is not a language-model neuron-pole audit or an explanation-scoring evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Ablation effects differ by layer: layers 3-6 pattern neurons promote their target moves on average, while layer 7 pattern neurons suppress them. Pattern-coverage results also depend on the neuron and F1-threshold restrictions.

fits_no_version.finding: Individual MLP neurons implement localized decision rules (L1N421 gated by L0N377) that do not generalize across board translations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a toy board-game transformer, single neurons implement position-specific logical rules.

fits_no_version.finding: 610 neurons classify unions of move-enabling board patterns with F1 > 0.99. These cover 75.2% of patterns (single-move neurons, F1 > 0.99) or 90.6% (all neurons, F1 > 0.9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In OthelloGPT, many mid-to-late MLP neurons are near-perfect classifiers of interpretable board patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: Pattern neuron ablations reduce target-move probability in layers 3-6 and raise it by about 15% in layer 7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpretable pattern neurons in OthelloGPT are causally relevant, with layer-dependent sign.

fits_no_version.finding: Clock neurons fire as a function of move number, apparently reading the positional encoding. The finding is anecdotal and has no row.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some OthelloGPT neurons encode game phase rather than board content.

fits_no_version.finding: A blank/not-blank circuit uses the direct embedding, layer-0 move-detector neurons and attention heads 0.2 and 0.3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: OthelloGPT computes cell occupancy with a recency-specific circuit.

record.problems: The analysis of the blank-cell circuit covers 50 examined games and does not establish that the circuit is exclusive. Some proposed attention-head behavior is explicitly conjectured but unchecked. The post reports no uncertainty estimates for the numerical results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results left out.

untested.parts: No share of interpretable neurons in any language model, dense or mixture-of-experts, or across scale.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron re-analysis.
No comparison of architecture, regularization or tools against interpretable-neuron share. The authors only speculate that smaller models might use superposition.
No neuron-based attribution graphs versus replacement models.
No held-out test of explanations from activating examples. The F1 classification is against ground-truth board patterns, not inspection-based explanations.

record.verdict_notes: OthelloGPT is a toy game-sequence model, not a language model, so V2 does not apply. The post reports no share of neurons that are interpretable overall. Its coverage percentages are shares of board patterns, not of neurons. The authors note the model may be oversized for the task, which limits any generalization to typical LLMs.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or estimates of neuron-pole job counts.
No audit of other language models, dense or mixture-of-experts models, or parameter scaling.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No comparison of architectures, regularization, interpretability tools, or estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
No attribution graphs or comparison with a trained replacement model and its reconstruction error.
No test of explanations against activation locations on examples not used to write them.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

relation.reason: It discusses neurons as clean classifiers in a toy model but does not test or use the claim. It cannot cite the later essay.

tranche.reason: Mechanistic study of OthelloGPT, an 8-layer, 25M-parameter Othello move model. It reports no share of neurons with one main job, no other-LM audit, no vision or attribution-graph or explanation-scoring result. It does not test any version.

source_check.notes: 75.2% and 90.6% are shares of the 1036 valid-move board patterns, not shares of neurons. 75.2% is for layers 4-6 only, and the 90.6% sentence most likely keeps that layer restriction but doesn't restate it. 610 is a neuron count with no total-neuron denominator. The study is an interim post, not peer-reviewed.

statements.correction: 610 neurons in the second half of the network predict a union of patterns with F1>0.99 (60k board states); no total-neuron denominator given. In layers 4, 5 and 6 only, single-move pattern neurons at F1>0.99 classify 75.2% of the 1036 valid-move board patterns. Relaxed to all neurons at F1>0.9: 90.6% of patterns classified.
statements.problem: All numbers are in the text, but the statement says the 610 neurons produce the 75.2% and 90.6% coverage. They don't. 610 is the count of F1>0.99 neurons in the second half of the network. 75.2% is for layers 4-6 only, using single-move neurons. 90.6% uses all neurons at the looser F1>0.9 threshold, not the 610.
